zoe: Heads-up — running extended canary for osmium14b (int4) against long-form summarization/QA. Hitting intermittent OOMs and noisy p95 spikes when clients request >700 tokens. Posting quick traces and configs.
omar: Can you paste the canary runtime config?
zoe: microbatch=1, batch=5, prefetch_window=192, prefetch_padding=0, max_new_tokens=1024 for the longform run. Artifact: s3://redwood-bench/osmium14b/int4/extended-2026-03-26
su: Worker stderr snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.3 GiB
Note: slab allocator could not find contiguous 768MB despite total_free=2.1GB
Stack: runtime/slab.cc:412 -> kv_store.cc:190 -> decoder.cc:88
Timeline: prefetch->kv_map_load->attn_kv_alloc->decode```
ben: That pattern screams contiguous allocation failure due to fragmentation. Quantized layout + aggressive prefetch creates lots of small slab allocations that later block large contiguous allocs.
zoe: Repro command: `./canary_run.sh --m osmium14b --quant int4 --prefetch 192 --max_new 1024 --requests 1000` gives ~2 OOMs / 1000. Changing to `--prefetch 48 --max_new 512` gives 0 OOMs in 1000.
omar: Proposal: conservative defaults for new int4 variants: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window<=64, prefetch_padding=32. Also add a short runtime compaction pass on allocation failure.
ben: I'm going to propose two runtime mitigations: (1) slab-compact-on-failure: when alloc fails, try compacting inactive slabs for up to 150ms then retry; (2) contiguous-fallback: if still fails, attempt to soft-evict oldest KV pages (configurable up to 25%) and retry. Both gated behind feature flags.
su: Also recommend an adaptive_prefetch strategy: base_window = 32, window = min(192, base + request_length/8) but with an upper bound on contiguous target bytes to avoid large single allocs. That will make prefetch proportional to context, preventing over-prefetch on short requests but keeping enough KV warm for long ones.
zoe: I ran a quick microbench with slab-compact enabled (feature flag on): p95 latency increased ~3% but OOMs dropped to 0 for the 1k run. ROUGE/BERTScore deltas vs fp16 are stable: ROUGE-L -3.1, BERTScore -0.015. chrF improved slightly for longform.
lina: Filed ML-1533: "osmium14b-int4: conservative defaults + slab-compact + adaptive_prefetch experiment".
deploy-bot: :rocket: starting canary deploy: osmium14b-int4 -> pool-canary-7
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary pod ready (v2026-03-26-int4-slabcompact)
omar: Plan: (1) set canary model config overrides: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch_window=48, prefetch_padding=32; (2) enable slab-compact feature flag on canary; (3) run 10k request sweep with metrics: p50/p95/p99, OOM count, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, chrF, cost per token; (4) if quality delta <= 2 pts and perf hit <=5%, consider promoting.
ben: I'll land the slab-compact PR and add telemetry to track compact attempts + reclaimed bytes. If compact frequency high, we'll revisit prefetch heuristics.
su: I'll coordinate the evaluation sweep and add an attention-pattern check to ensure quant compression artifacts aren't showing up as repeated n-grams.
zoe: Thanks all — I'll post the sweep artifacts and flag any regressions. Short-term: keeping prod int4 defaults conservative. :thumbsup:
